title: Expand short-id/self-id sugar to a canonical issue address via kind inference
description:
One address form is sugar: `<short-id>/<self-id>` (e.g. `56ab0224/REQ-01`) must expand to the canonical issue form `@/issue/<short-id>/<kind>/<self-id>` by inferring `kind` from which configured kind's `id-pattern` regex matches `<self-id>` — no code path does this today (`split_qualified_id` just treats the whole thing as an opaque self-id).

Inference applies ONLY to issue-scoped kinds (`scope = "issue"` in `[item_kinds]`, e.g. this repo's `requirement`, `decision`, `risk`) — project-scoped kinds (e.g. `invariant`, `definition`, and any future registry-first kind) require the explicit kind segment and have no sugar form, because their self-ids are free-form slugs with no distinguishing shape.

Add a pure domain-layer expansion function taking the sugar string plus the configured kind list as a parameter — mirroring how `resolve_item_kinds` (`domain/item.rs:1219-1233`) takes the kind registry as a parameter rather than hardcoding kind names — that:
1. Filters the kind list to issue-scoped kinds only.
2. Finds every issue-scoped kind whose `id_pattern` regex matches `<self-id>` (the same `id_pattern.find` mechanism `extract_raw_items` already uses at `domain/item.rs:870`).
3. Exactly one match: expands to `(Scope::Issue(short_id), matched_kind_name, self_id)` — the triple shape produced by the address parser.
4. Zero matches: returns a clear typed error (self-id matches no configured issue-scoped kind's pattern).
5. More than one match: returns a clear typed error naming every ambiguous candidate kind — never silently picks the first.

This does not touch any resolver call site; that is separate, later work.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: a sugar string whose self-id matches exactly one issue-scoped kind's `id_pattern` (e.g. `D-1` against this repo's `decision` kind pattern `D-[0-9]+`, or `RISK-1` against `risk`'s `RISK-[0-9]+`) expands to `(Scope::Issue(short_id), "decision"/"risk", self_id)`; covered by unit tests for at least two distinct issue-scoped kinds.
- [hard] REQ-02: a sugar string whose self-id matches NO issue-scoped kind's `id_pattern` returns a distinct typed error (not the ambiguous-match error); covered by a unit test.
- [hard] REQ-03: a sugar string whose self-id matches MORE THAN ONE issue-scoped kind's `id_pattern` (construct two issue-scoped test kinds with deliberately overlapping patterns) returns a typed error naming every matching candidate kind, verified by a unit test asserting the error lists all matched kind names.
- [hard] REQ-04: project-scoped kinds (`scope = "project"`) are excluded from candidate matching regardless of whether their `id_pattern` would otherwise match, verified by a unit test using a project-scoped kind whose pattern matches the input self-id but is correctly not selected.
